correctness.rationale: Reconstruction: group of order 2q implies nonresidues minus -1; reflection and six elementary quadratic character sums give the exact integer quartic sum after the explicitly checked root correction; disjoint -1 alignments give E_p(d). Squarefree degree-four Weil estimate forces baseline B_p>4 for p>=113. The finite residue range is exhausted for every safe p<113 and every x,d by standalone integer-arithmetic code; p=23 fails and all p>=47 pass. Tests up to 1000 merely corroborate the analytic universal argument.

originality.rationale: Compared published primitive-root configuration theorems by logical implication, not wording. The 2014 paper is the archival motivating question; the 2021 exact exception theorem covers d=1, not all d, and the 2019 offset paper gives asymptotic context, not exact sharp safe-prime prescribed-step counts. Literature coverage is necessarily incomplete and the residual risks are stated.

value.rationale: The exact every-nonzero-d existence at sharp safe-prime cutoff 47 resolves a motivated part of the four-term primitive-root configuration problem beyond known unit-step existence. The formula exposes an arithmetic invariant and the sole obstruction (-1), with a mathematically necessary finite boundary census. This is neither a mere restatement of the older d=1 theorem nor an arbitrary isolated computation.
